Even the tablecloths did not appear to be changed after previous guests left; they were simply turned over and used again. The staff service, however, was good and friendly. One particular highlight was the gözleme — probably the best I have ever had during all my years of holidays in Turkey. The lady making them had such beautiful, kind eyes that seemed to radiate warmth and love, and you could feel the same warmth in the gözleme she prepared. Beautiful location, only 30 minutes from the airport. Staff were friendly throughout — funnily enough they got noticeably nicer after the first week, like they'd been sent on a customer service refresher mid-stay. Sun beds were never really an issue; plenty available if you were down by 9am. Restaurant seating was always easy to find too, no scrapping for tables. The Kids Club was the highlight for us — genuinely excellent. Our daughter didn't need any persuading; she was raring to go every single morning. We'd also strongly recommend the Brothers boat trip, run by the guys at Duja — a brilliant trip, and they were genuinely pleasant, still greeting us and having a chat every time we crossed paths for the rest of the holiday. A special mention for our Jet2 rep, Hakan — we ran into a few issues during the stay and he was fantastic at sorting them out for us. A few things let it down. The food was repetitive and, frankly, a bit boring — the same rotation day after day, and it would have gone a long way to have a themed night or two to break it up. The daytime pool and mini disco music didn't change once in two weeks, which got old fast. The à la carte experience, which is talked up as something special, really wasn't — didn't feel any different to the main buffet in quality. And the hotel itself is showing its age; it needs some general refurbishment and TLC. Some floors in the main hotel also have shared terraces with only a limited sea view, worth checking before you book. Overall: great spot, brilliant kids' facilities, a top boat trip and a rep who had our back, but the food, entertainment, and upkeep need investment to match the location.

The buffet was very good, although after 12 days it did inevitably start to feel a little repetitive. I particularly enjoyed the **yoga sessions**, which were a lovely addition to the day and made even better by the beautiful setting. We’ve just come back from a 2 weeks stay at Duja Bodrum and overall we had a really great holiday. We’d definitely go back. The transfer from the airport only took about 25mins. The food was one of the things we really enjoyed. There was loads of choice and the snack bars were particularly good, with different pasta dishes, chicken wraps, burgers, pizzas, waffles etc. Breakfast was also really good, with omelettes made to order as well as lots of other options. There was always food being cooked fresh outside at tea time as well as the buffet, which was great. We tried the Asian and fish à la carte restaurants and both were really nice. The food was lovely and the service was great. One thing we really liked was that there are freezers with ice creams dotted around the hotel, as well as fridges full of bottled water, so you can just help yourself whenever you want. The lifeguards were also really on the ball around the pools, which was reassuring. The ladies in the kids’ club were lovely. We personally never left our children there on their own and always stayed with them, but from what we saw they were fantastic with all the children and really looked after them. Selin & Nehir deserves a special mention, our boys loved them. The boys are wild and they were amazing with them. Customer service throughout the hotel was probably one of the biggest positives. Everyone was really friendly and helpful and they genuinely couldn’t do enough for you. Our room was clean and spacious and the maid did a really good job. The mini bar was also restocked every day, which was a nice bonus. If I had one criticism, it would be that I’d have liked a few more evening shows. They had shows about four nights a week, and on the other nights there was a film for the kids, bingo or a night off. The shows they did have were really good and the mini disco was on every night, so there was still plenty going on, but more evening entertainment would have been nice. They do also have live music at the pool bar each night. Overall, we really enjoyed our stay. There’s a great choice of food, the staff are lovely, the hotel is well looked after and there’s plenty for families. We had a brilliant holiday and would definitely return to Duja Bodrum.

While there were some excellent aspects of the holiday, there were several areas that fell well below what we would expect from a 5-star hotel. The biggest disappointment was the food. We booked an à la carte restaurant under the impression that we would be able to choose from five different restaurants. However, when it came to booking, we were only offered a choice between the Turkish or Fish restaurant. Neither appealed to us, but we opted for the Turkish restaurant. The food arrived cold, the presentation was poor, and it felt like very little care had gone into the dining experience. The main restaurant was also disappointing and certainly not the “amazing” dining experience described in many reviews. We are not fussy eaters by any means, but there were several evenings where the only things that looked appetising were chicken nuggets, chips, salad and dessert. The food seemed to be catered more towards German and Russian guests, with surprisingly few authentic Turkish dishes available. If there had been restaurants within walking distance of the hotel, we would have chosen to eat elsewhere on several occasions. The snack bars at lunchtime were much better. A lot of the food appeared to be frozen products, but it was generally edible and some items were genuinely enjoyable. Service in the main restaurant was another let-down. Staff always seemed attentive to guests of other nationalities, whereas as English guests we often struggled to get service. On more than one occasion we had nearly finished our meal before anyone came to take a drinks order. On a positive note, the entertainment team were outstanding. They were always friendly, welcoming and enthusiastic, and genuinely couldn’t do enough for guests. The reception team were also polite and helpful throughout our stay. In fact, the majority of the staff were excellent and always willing to help. We really couldn’t fault their attitude. If you tip them, be prepared to have drinks arriving constantly! The accommodation was another major disappointment. Our room felt very tired and nowhere near the standard expected of a 5-star hotel. There were large cracks in the bathroom tiles, peeling paint on the ceiling from what appeared to be a previous leak, stained bedroom furnishings, wallpaper that was peeling away with mould and dirty marks visible, and bed sheets with holes and stains. The minibar was supposed to be replenished daily but was only restocked three times during our seven-night stay, despite us reporting the issue to reception. Our biggest issue was the room we were initially allocated. We were placed in a Club Room, which honestly felt more like a 3-star property. Apart from being in a quieter area, there was very little positive to say about it. It looked dated, lacked privacy, had a tiny balcony, and both the bedroom and bathroom were in poor condition. Duja is a truly massive resort with expansive grounds, offering plenty of space to explore and enjoy. When we first arrived, it made a fantastic impression — the setting is beautiful, and during the early part of our stay, it felt relaxed and well-balanced. There were plenty of sun loungers available, with lots of quiet spots to unwind and soak up the sun. However, as the week went on, the experience began to shift. The hotel became noticeably more crowded, and it unfortunately felt as though the resort wasn’t quite equipped to handle the influx of guests. Finding a comfortable area to relax became much more difficult, and the restaurant in particular suffered — lunch and dinner times were consistently overcrowded and far from enjoyable. The rooms and facilities, while functional, are starting to show their age and would benefit from some refurbishment and modernisation. A bit of TLC would go a long way in elevating the overall experience. To top it off, we had the misfortune of being next to a very loud neighbour who partied on their balcony until well past midnight, which took away from the otherwise relaxing atmosphere we were hoping for. Overall, Duja has great potential thanks to its size and location, but it currently struggles during busier periods and would benefit from some updates and better crowd management.

We recently returned from a week-long holiday with a group of 4 adults and 5 children (ages 10-13). This hotel has plenty of potential, but a major security issue and subpar standards mean it does not deserve its 5-star rating. The Good Points: *Pools & Beach: The main pool is large, the indoor pool was great during poor weather, and the beach is very nice. There were always plenty of sunbeds available. *Staff: The team was generally friendly, though we frequently had to use Google Translate as very few spoke English. *Room Resolution: When we pointed out that our third room was smelly and unkept, the staff accommodated us and moved us near our other two clean, spacious rooms. The Bad Points: *Late Arrival: Arriving at 23:30, the restaurant was shut and no arrival buffet was set up. We had to ask multiple times just to get basic sandwiches.Room *Maintenance: In our moving room, the air conditioning and television did not work at all in any of our rooms. We also had no Wi-Fi in our rooms for the first few days, which was rectified after complaining everyday. *Mobility Warning: The hotel is massive and dotted with steps everywhere. Avoid this property if you have mobility struggles. *Crowd Management: Meal times are incredibly chaotic, and the staff clearly struggle to manage the volume of guests. *The Major Concern (Data Protection Breach):At check-in, we provided names and phone numbers for the adults in each room. The next morning, every single number received a text from a local tour company claiming to be our official holiday reps. They sold us trips that we later had to cancel and refund. Our holiday provider confirmed they have no reps in Turkey. When we confronted the hotel about leaking our data, they denied it and blamed our private airport transfer. However, we caught them out: one adult had accidentally written a child’s name next to their phone number on the hotel check-in card. The tour company addressed that adult by the child's name, proving without a doubt that the leak came directly from the hotel front desk. The hotel still refuses to take responsibility for what is a serious breach of privacy and a potential police matter. Without this security issue, we would have rated this a 3-star hotel. Because of it, we cannot recommend this place to anyone and will not be back.

The younger children are enjoying the kids club. The indoor pool is good when we need to give the children a break from the sun. Several of our family has massages(extra cost) they gave us very good reports. We used our 1 night a la carte to eat at the Italian restaurant and it made a nice change. Lots of reviews mentioned mosquitos,so we brought lots of products but were not using them as no mosquitos at first but later in the week some of us did get bitten by something. There is a bit of walking between club area & main building but we find it is good exercise and the golf buggies are always parked at the door near reception and the guys there were willing to drive us if we asked. There is a very handy what's app number that one can message during one's stay to ask questions about the resort. All the mom's got a flower and beautiful letter on Mother's day. The hotel wifi was very helpful, especially because we were outside eu roaming. No coverage in some areas but it .Just be challenging to 100% cover such a large area. As our week progressed the resort got more and more busy, the crowds made our stay less pleasant but overall its 5 stars for Duja Bodrum. Thank you all for our great holiday

We stayed at this hotel in May and had a wonderful experience. The service staff were excellent — always friendly, helpful, and professional. The food was very good with a great variety every day. The hotel territory is large, beautiful, and very well maintained. The beach is clean and well organized, with a wide shoreline and comfortable access to the sea. There are daily entertainment activities for children, and in the evenings adults can enjoy quizzes, concerts, and other fun programs. The hotel also has a SPA center. I had a medical massage there, and the massage therapist HACER is a true professional. I highly recommend her. There is also a leather shop in the hotel called LojaMax. The seller Arif was extremely helpful, explained everything clearly, and organized transportation to and from the store. There is absolutely no reason to be afraid to visit — the shop staff are very kind and welcoming. We truly enjoyed our stay and will definitely return to this hotel again!

All hotel and facilities extremely clean. Hardworking and friendly staff. Highly recommended. Cleanliness is outstanding. Could add fruit to restaurant and a different option evening. Great value for money. Clean rooms. Good quiet location, can get a taxi to centre.
Amazing Hotel! All the staff made the experience especially Sefa, Rio & Ayaz and all the bar staff Will be back
Fabulous hotel, big shout out to Sefa, Rio and Ayaz, but all the staff were amazing ⭐️⭐️⭐️ will definitely be back!

Doja Hotel in Bodrum was a fantastic experience. All the staff were very friendly and welcoming, and the level of hospitality was excellent. Everything was handled on time and in an organized way, which made us feel very satisfied throughout our stay. There were various activities at different times of the day, and the entertainment program was very well planned. The music, especially the DJ, was excellent and really created a great atmosphere. The food and drinks were also of very high quality, and overall everything was outstanding. The staff responded quickly to any requests, and it was clear that guest satisfaction was very important to them. We had a wonderful time and many great moments during our stay. If you are planning to travel to Bodrum and want to spend your holiday in an excellent hotel, I would definitely recommend this hotel.

My intial thoughts when arriving was this resort was very nice and i arrived at night so ofcourse excited of the views to come in day light. The reason for the 4 star is because the room that had been provided did not reflect the standards of the resort. The room looked average. As i walked in i noticed a weird smell and the room was really cold. The thermostat that controls the temperature was not working. i noticed in the corner damp/mould and with a 7 month old baby i requested a room change as this is not healthy for a baby. management were quick to provide us another room that was close to reception but uphill so wasn’t convenient however the room was a lot better than the first and we decided to stay. After this experience, everything else was faultless. Staff were friendly, starbucks was great and the starbucks employee was very quick and very friendly. Buggie service available. Quality of Food was good, more variety offered when the resort got busier. the views were amazing. Other than the room we initially had, i would recommend the resort. Chilled atmosphere. Quick note: there is a concierge desk near reception area. You are advised to go there for taxi and they give price, however taxi rank not far from main gate area, they offer taxi on the meter.
Nice & clean hotel & very good service Near the airport very nice views, bonus it was not very busy, food was great & all staff was very friendly/helpful, all in all very good holiday

Amazing resort with lots of great facilities of pool, SPA and water slides. Food was available nearly ever hour of the day as breakfast, lunch and dinner were for long hours with snacks in between. Quality of food is good if not excellent but desserts were the highlight of the main meals. The only thing I wish they could have done better is to have more English speaking staff as it’s difficult to communicate. Also, better quality of bedding as there were no duvets just scratchy sheets.

There are no shops nearby, and it takes about 20 minutes to drive to the nearest town. Room cleaning was quite poor, especially during our stay with a child. There was mold in the bathroom, which was disappointing. The kids’ activities start only at 9 p.m., which is far too late for young children. The food was generally good, although there was very little seafood offered.

Review as a couple visiting in September. Firstly, the views are amazing. The location of the hotel is easy via taxi from the airport, and the scenery is stunning as it is situated on a hillside. Pros: - no subbed wars (maybe due to end of season) but as there are spaces along the pier, beach, promenade and up at the pool there are loads of sunbeds around, even when arriving later in the morning. - Starbucks is a really nice touch, it is simple (lattes and refresher drinks) but adds a little bit of home for those who enjoy it. - the hotel is very clean, there are always cleaners on hand, clean tables and the rooms were spotless. - the village room I would recommend! We were in the middle of the village, and didn’t hear too much, however I can see that if you are unfortunate and get a room further away it’s a longer walk to the hotel, or too close and the music would keep you awake if you wanted an early night. - the sea! Wow wow wow!! There are safe spaces to swim, and if you are confident I’d recommend going SUP in the early morning. Bring snorkels or goggles are there are lots of fish to look at when swimming. Cons: - the food. If you are a foodie (of which we are) we struggled. Very repetitive, same starters and desserts every day. Very stew heavy and a lot of beige. After 10 days we’re very bored of the same thing each time. The A La Carte restaurant (Chinese, Italian or Fish) were very nice and much more what we expected for what we paid - this just was a disappointment for our trip. - dinner service was busy, if you can go later in the evening I’d reccomend you do. At 7pm and only one dinner restaurant there were long queues to wait, limited tables and slow to get drinks from staff. - the branded drinks are only served in once place … why?? At all the bars you can get drinks (cocktails are always good) but the branded spirits are only served in the lobby bar, which limited seating (but amazing views) it was a shame as we felt we had to battle for seats to enjoy a nicer drink. - music on repeat - all the time. We love some music while chilling by the pool, but the same playlist is used everyday, there are only so many times we could listen to Ellie Goulding and Coldplay before you get bored. There are a few quiet spaces but not many, go further down the beach to get away from the music. Overall, we had a lovely time and adapted to what we wanted to make the most of what we paid for.

We recently stayed at Duja Bodrum and overall had a great experience. The hotel is kept very clean, and there are plenty of hardworking staff who are always friendly and helpful. The food was very good with lots of variety, and the à la carte restaurant was definitely the highlight meal of the week. The kids really enjoyed the children’s pool and water slides, and the afternoon snack bars were a nice touch. It’s also handy that the hotel offers a midnight meal, which is great if you arrive late or get hungry after hours. Our room was spacious and comfortable too. The beachfront is lovely and relaxing — during our stay, the public beach just to the right of the hotel was completely empty, which made the setting even better. A few things to be aware of: the resort is large and spread out across different levels, so you’ll often need to use stairs or lifts to get around. The snack bar by the slide pool was closed all week during our stay, and the slides only opened for a few hours each day — this may have been due to it being a quieter period. There’s also about a 5-minute walk between the slides and the kids’ pool, which could be tricky with younger children. Around the pool and resort, be prepared to be approached fairly often by the brothers selling boat trips, as well as the hotel photographers. One other point is transport into Bodrum. Reception directed us towards a taxi service charging €60, but we later found out there’s a bus just outside the hotel that only costs €3 return — a much better option for guests to know about! Despite these minor drawbacks, we had a very enjoyable stay. The staff really do make the difference, and we’d happily recommend Duja Bodrum and would return in the future.

Not a 5 star experience Unfortunately I can’t say this hotel matches its 5 star status. There were some positives: - the pool area is great, no fight for sunbeds at all but this may have been because it was September. - the beach area is also really nice and the seafood restaurant at night was absolutely fabulous - the room was cleaned everyday with no problems However, overall we were quite disappointed, especially with the food. The buffet doesn’t change much each day and my partner found that there was never really much meat on offer. I found the selection extremely beige with pasta, fried food, chips, and more carbs on offer every single night. There just wasn’t many appealing options at all. We actually resorted to eating out in Bodrum, which unfortunately was extremely expensive so be aware of high prices. To get to bodrum the hotel try to offer you a transfer of €50 return - do not take it. A yellow cab is 600 Lira / 13 euros. We were only staying for a week and you are only granted 1 meal at one of the restaurants in the hotel, which is a shame. The room was adequate but very worn and tired. There is no iron in the room (they charge extra to iron anything). In general, we did not find the staff friendly at all, and did not at all feel welcome throughout the hotel. The only staff member who was friendly was ayaz at the Starbucks cafe - he works extremely hard on his own. The drinks are also really inconsistent across all the bars. If you’re looking for a “wow” 5 star, this isn’t the one.
My family enjoyed very much excellent service and facilities we definitely book holiday again

The hotel is excellent , very big, has everything in it with amazing views, we liked the village rooms and the walking around, and the working staff were nice. The food is very good, although almost same menu everyday with no variety. Since i suffer from some food allergies, i had some issues with it, even though the food at the hotel labeled with allergy signs, not everything was labeled correctly and clearly, and the staff didn’t always know how to help or answer me.
Vacances et détente Le séjour était formidable. Chambre correcte, personnel très sympa et formidable. Bonne restauration, idéal pour les familles. Plage magnifique et piscine grandiose.
Sauberkeit und Personal sind super und Speiseauswahl war super
